title: Refactor streaming example: consistent delta handling + final assembly + better error branches
author: Dana Lo
description:
Context
Our TS streaming example had drifted from the canonical event-handling conventions we’re standardizing across Python/TS/Go. In particular:
- We were printing partial deltas directly (fine for demo) but not demonstrating correct final message assembly.
- We treated “final” events inconsistently (some models emit both a final message and a final text chunk; our example would double-print).
- Errors/disconnects were handled via a generic catch, which hid actionable debug signals for users.

This PR refactors the example into a single, readable consumer loop that:
- Assembles the final assistant message deterministically from deltas.
- Uses explicit branches per event type with consistent logging.
- Shows safe handling of partial tool-call arguments (log + defer parsing until final) without implying unsupported semantics.
- Adds an abort/timeout path and clearer error messaging for common streaming failures.

What changed
- Introduced a small helper (Accumulator) to collect text deltas and track “final” state.
- Refactored the streaming consumer loop to switch on event type and avoid double-printing.
- Added structured logging prefixes to make console output easier to follow in docs/code tabs.
- Added explicit branches for:
  - stream aborted by user (AbortError)
  - network disconnect / retryable error (with guidance)
  - server-side error event emitted mid-stream
- Updated README snippet to match the new example output and recommended pattern.

Notes
- This PR does not change API surface area; it is example-only (plus a tiny internal helper in the examples folder).
- We intentionally do not parse/JSON.parse tool-call arguments during streaming; we only log partial args and note that users should wait for the completed tool call.

Screenshots / sample output
Before: mixed console output, sometimes duplicated final message
After:
[stream] started request_id=rw_...
[delta] "Hel"
[delta] "lo"
[final] assistant_message="Hello" tokens_in=... tokens_out=...

Follow-ups
- Golden transcript fixtures are tracked in ENG-4822 (separate PR).

examples(streaming): refactor event loop into explicit event-type branches
docs(readme): update streaming snippet + expected output
examples(streaming): add abort/timeout + improved error messages
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we make it impossible to double-print finals? I’ve seen models emit both a final delta and a final message. Suggest tracking a single “completed” flag and only rendering the assembled content once.

Dana Lo (author): Yep—added `completed` to the accumulator and gated both `message.completed` and `response.completed` handling. Also added a debug log if we see a second completion event, so users can file a repro without confusion.

Brian Murphy (review): Error handling: please distinguish AbortError vs server error event. Also in the disconnect branch, avoid suggesting automatic retries unless we can guarantee idempotency. Maybe say “you may retry if your app can tolerate duplicates; include request_id for support”.

Dana Lo (author): Updated catch branches: AbortError => user-cancelled, TypeError/network => “connection dropped”. Added text about duplicates and including request_id + time window when contacting support.
Monica Patel (review): Logging is better, but can we keep it copy/paste friendly for docs tabs? Prefer stable prefixes and minimal noise. Also, avoid `console.debug` since some environments hide it.
Dana Lo (author): Switched to `console.log` with `[stream]/[delta]/[final]/[error]` prefixes. Removed extra per-event JSON dumps; kept a single line for tool-call partial args with truncation.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI failed on first run (lint). Looks like a trailing comma / unused import in the new helper.
Dana Lo (author): Fixed lint + reran. Also pinned the example tsconfig to avoid differing moduleResolution defaults across Node versions in CI.
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Looks aligned with the event model conventions. Thanks for the note about not parsing tool args mid-stream—this matches the support learnings from SUP-18421.
Brian Murphy (approval): Approved with the retry wording changes.
Monica Patel (approval): Approved. Please ensure ENG-4824 references this PR for the parity matrix.
release_notes: TypeScript streaming example now demonstrates consistent delta handling and final message assembly.
Improved logging and clearer error branches (abort vs disconnect vs server error).
README snippet updated to match canonical streaming conventions.
